explanation: Its buildings rest on wooden piles driven deep into the lagoon's mud, where the lack of oxygen keeps them from rotting.

claims.text: Venice is built on islands in a lagoon, with canals in place of many streets.
Florence, Naples and Genoa are not built on islands in a lagoon.
Many of Venice's buildings rest on wooden piles driven into the mud of the lagoon.
The waterlogged mud has little oxygen, which slows the rotting of Venice's wooden piles.

evidence.restatement: Venice is built on islands in a lagoon, with canals doing the job of streets.
Florence, Naples and Genoa are mainland cities, not lagoon islands.
Venice's buildings stand on wooden piles driven into the lagoon mud.
The oxygen-poor waterlogged mud slows the piles' decay.
Venice is built on islands in a lagoon and uses canals for much of its transport.
Florence, Naples and Genoa are not built on a lagoon.
Many of Venice's buildings rest on wooden piles driven into the lagoon mud.
The waterlogged mud has little oxygen, which slows the decay of the buried wooden piles.

issues.note: The stem says Venice 'uses canals instead of streets'. Venice has narrow streets (calli) as well as canals, so this is poetic exaggeration. No option can compete (Florence, Naples and Genoa have no lagoon canals), so there is no second answer. 'Uses canals as its main streets' would be literally safer. No change needed.
